result.topic_en: Euler simplifies his formula for the efflux velocity of water through a tube with friction, using an experimental friction coefficient of about 1/4000, examines the limiting cases of a very small orifice and a fully open tube, and argues that the apparent paradox of friction increasing the velocity arises because the water does not adhere to the tube everywhere.
result.transcription:
356 TENTAMEN THEORIAE

48. Quantum autem ex craſſis quibusdam experimentis obiter tantum colligere licuit, valor ipſius $\alpha$ prodiit circiter $=\frac{1}{4000}$. Hinc dummodo numerus $\frac{b}{g}$ notabiliter fuerit minor, quam 4000, ſufficiet in primis terminis ſubſtitiſſe, ita vt ſit
$v\left(1-\frac{\alpha b}{g}\cdot\frac{k^4}{g^4}\right)=a+b-\frac{\alpha b}{g}\left(a+\frac{1}{2}b+l\right)$, ſeu
$v=a+b-\frac{\alpha b}{g}\left(a+\frac{1}{2}b+l-\frac{k^4}{g^4}(a+b)\right)$.

49. Si orificium $CC=kk$ fuerit minimum, ita vt $\frac{k^4}{g^4}$ pro nihilo haberi poſſit, erit
$v=a+b-\frac{\alpha b}{g}\left(a+\frac{1}{2}b+l\right)$.
ſin autem tubus infra plane ſit apertus, ſeu $gg=kk$, habebitur
$v=a+b-\frac{\alpha b}{g}\left(l-\frac{1}{2}b\right)$.
Illo ergo caſu celeritas effluxus eſt minima, atque a frictione maxime impeditur; hoc autem caſu videtur fieri poſſe, vt fiat $v=a+b$, perinde ac ſi nulla frictio adeſſet.

50. Hoc ſcilicet euenire deberet, ſi $b=2l$, ſeu cum ſit $l$ triginta pedum, ſi $b=60$ pedum: atque adeo, ſi eſſet $b>60$ pedum, calculus noſter praeberet $v>a+b$. Interim tamen certiſſimum eſt, frictionem in cauſa eſſe non poſſe, vt aqua maiori celeritate exſiliat, quam ſi nulla adeſſet frictio. Dico igitur, huiusmodi caſus ideo locum habere non poſſe, propterea quod aqua tubo non vbique adhaereat; ſed vacuum relinquat, ita, vt calculus ad eos accommodari nequeat.

51. Quod

items.english: The value of alpha, as far as could be gathered from certain rough experiments, came out to about 1/4000.

items.quote: Interim tamen certiſſimum eſt, frictionem in cauſa eſſe non poſſe, vt aqua maiori celeritate exſiliat, quam ſi nulla adeſſet frictio.
items.english: Meanwhile it is most certain that friction cannot be the cause of water spurting out with greater velocity than if there were no friction.

items.quote: Dico igitur, huiusmodi caſus ideo locum habere non poſſe, propterea quod aqua tubo non vbique adhaereat; ſed vacuum relinquat, ita, vt calculus ad eos accommodari nequeat.
items.english: I say therefore that such cases cannot occur, because the water does not adhere to the tube everywhere but leaves a vacuum, so that the calculation cannot be applied to them.
